feedback: If a learner selects £10 as the sale price, confirm the discount is right but ask what remains: £40 − £10 = £30.
If a learner selects £25, revisit per-cent-means-per-hundred: 25% of £40 is a quarter of 40 = £10, not £25.

If a learner writes 60 ÷ 100 or 60 ÷ 20 and presents it as 20% of 60, connect the divisor to the fraction: 1% = ÷100 (so 60 ÷ 100 = 0.6 is one per cent), then 20% = 20 of those = 12; or 20% = 1/5 = ÷5, not ÷20.
If a learner can only reach an answer one way, prompt a benchmark route (e.g. 10% then double) to build flexibility.
activities.intendedInsight: Fluent recall of the equivalents must combine with the context subtract-step: finding the discount is not the same as finding the sale price.
learnerActions: Match the three equivalent forms: 1/5 ↔ 20% ↔ 0.2 and 3/4 ↔ 75% ↔ 0.75.
Complete fill-in-the-blank computations such as '20% of 60 = __' and '1/5 of 60 = __'.
Answer a contextual item: a shop offers 25% off a £40 item — what is the sale price? Watch for the trap of £10 (that is the discount, not the price) and £25 (base-neglect, '25% off = £25').
Explain, for at least one item, a second route to the same answer (e.g. 20% of 60 via 10% of 60 doubled).
activities.title: Fluency and context-step rehearsal
